recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: Modulatory score-bias selection authority at E3.select
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: Modulatory/secondary score-bias channels (MECH-314 curiosity bonus, MECH-320 vigor no-op penalty) are added to candidate scores at e3.select but are dominated by the primary harm/goal score term, so they never change argmax (604a bias=0.0 even ON, 624a v_t=0.05 both ON==OFF). Give modulatory biases competitive selection authority -- score normalization before bias addition, relative scaling of the bias to the candidate score gap, or a separate arbitration/gating channel -- so an enabled modulatory mechanism can change selection. Mirrors the z_goal-vs-harm salience gap (603e/626a/622) and the monostrategy 'diversity must act at/after E3 scoring' finding.
depends_on_unresolved: ARC-065 behavioral diversity (same E3.select arbitration layer)

cluster_pattern.shape: Substrate-operative / negative-control criterion passes (mechanism machinery confirmed firing), but the mechanism produces no distinguishable effect on measured behaviour -- ON == OFF.
cluster_pattern.structural_property: 604a + 624a: a modulatory/secondary additive score-bias (curiosity bonus, vigor no-op penalty) does not reach E3 action selection with enough authority to change argmax against the dominant primary (harm/goal) score term. Same phenomenon as the z_goal-vs-harm salience gap (603e/626a/622) and the monostrategy 'diversity must act at/after E3 scoring' finding. 630 is in the same family (mechanism effect not isolable in the ecological regime) but via a distinct proximate cause -- an environment confound, not bias-propagation -- and routes separately.
